headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage via shared filesystem/MCP; Cline’s broad workspace access can contaminate MemMachine’s context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, and its state is shared via filesystem; MemMachine also uses MCP and ingests conversational context. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Cline writes attacker-controlled content that MemMachine later treats as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is documented in both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Cline writes prompt-like content into a workspace file that MemMachine later reads through MCP or API input
IF MemMachine treats retrieved file or conversation content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Disable MCP file-reading paths for MemMachine
Add a provenance tag to any file passed between agents
Review Cline outputs before MemMachine consumes them
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If they share a filesystem or MCP bridge, sensitive code or screenshots can flow into MemMachine’s memory layer or out through Cline’s networked tools. The profiles show the necessary surfaces, but not a direct leak, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP resource
IF Cline is allowed to transmit file contents or screenshots to external services
IF MemMachine persists imported context beyond the session
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Turn off screenshot sharing unless needed
Limit Cline network egress to approved endpoints
Purge MemMachine memory after each task
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on shared inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities; MemMachine exposes REST/Python/MCP interfaces that can also mutate shared state if wired that way. Because Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem and neither profile shows locking, concurrent writes or git-state corruption are plausible in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty about MemMachine’s write scope pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF MemMachine is configured to write back through its API or MCP server
IF two instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use per-agent branches or directories
Add a file lock around shared outputs
Pause MemMachine writes during Cline edits
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; MemMachine can consume conversational context and act as a planning layer. If MemMachine treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream plans or stored memory. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous action-taking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Cline-generated text without verification
IF Cline’s browser-derived claims are stored as durable memory
IF downstream workflows act on MemMachine’s stored facts
mitigations: Require human review of Cline outputs before storage
Mark browser-derived claims as untrusted
Add a verification step before MemMachine writes memory
Limit MemMachine to read-only mode for Cline outputs
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If regulated or sensitive data is routed from Cline into MemMachine’s persistent memory, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the safest supported judgment is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Cline and then persisted by MemMachine
IF MemMachine retention exceeds the operator’s policy for the same data class
IF screenshots or secrets are stored in long-term memory
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Set a short retention window for MemMachine
Redact screenshots before transfer
Document which data classes may be persisted
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
